previousDisplay.cause: The overall average of 5.95 was rounded to one decimal and labeled as current GPA without distinguishing accumulated results.

calculationAndSyncFixes: Use one shared calculation for profile, progress and AI context; display both scales and both aggregate scopes to two decimal places.
Preserve the original numeric IU scale-4 score before falling back to letter conversion.
Keep P/NP records while excluding them from GPA; allow missing numeric results without inventing a zero score or letter grade.
Keep learning/exam attempts and select the latest completed result per subject chronologically for accumulated totals.
Preserve transcript attempts in detailed history; repeated migration and sync do not duplicate results.
Overall averages include failed graded credits; cumulative means use passed graded credits; the semester scale-10 recap uses passed graded credits.
Do not infer the total program credits from downloaded subjects or hardcode a program total.

aiHistoricalComparison.previousLimitation: Raw grade rows could be limited or removed when chat context was reduced, and prompts did not consistently request earlier-semester comparisons.
implemented: Calculate academicHistory from the full synced transcript before applying raw grade limits.
Include overall totals, chronological semester summaries, previous/latest term changes, retakes and subjects needing review.
Retain academicHistory through chat context reduction; bound long arrays and report truncation.
Request earlier-versus-latest semester comparisons in chat, study/exam planning and progress advice while distinguishing GPA scales and scopes.
Use server transcript totals rather than client-supplied academicHistory; accept equivalent decimal commas in supported numeric claims.
Treat grades as historical results rather than a fixed judgment of ability; do not invent scores for ungraded subjects.

verification.note: Test groups overlap and must not be summed as a unique test count. Write tests use synthetic fixtures and temporary databases.
